title: Expected findings for a corpus case
description: The contract for one test design in tests/corpus. This file is what makes the verification suite itself testable: a check is not trusted until a known-bad case proves it fires and a known-good case proves it does not false-positive. Adding a check without a corpus case is not allowed.

design.description: Directory name of the case. Must match its folder so a mismatch is caught rather than silently testing the wrong design.

defect_injected.description: For known_bad cases: the single defect deliberately introduced, in plain language. Each case injects exactly one defect so a firing check proves that specific detection rather than a general smell.

derived_from.description: The known_good case this was copied from. Keeping the diff to one defect is what makes the fixture reviewable.

exhaustive.description: When true, findings beyond those expected fail the test. Known-good cases set this with an empty expect list to assert a genuinely clean run.

expect.description: Findings that MUST be produced. Matching is on stable fields (check_id, code, component), never on message wording.

message_contains.description: Optional substring assertion. Use sparingly: matching on prose makes tests brittle.

why.description: Why a correct checker must report this. Documents intent for whoever debugs a regression later.

forbid.description: Findings that must NOT appear, e.g. asserting a defect does not trigger unrelated checks.

not_yet_detected.description: Defects known to be present that no implemented check catches yet. Recorded rather than deleted so the corpus tracks real coverage gaps instead of hiding them; tests report these as expected gaps and fail if one starts passing silently.

then.description: A known_bad case must state its defect and must assert at least one finding or record why none is detected yet.
A known_good case exists to catch false positives, so it must assert exhaustively that nothing fires.
